indication_pass.question: Known lung nodule under surveillance, admitted with fever: has the nodule changed?
indication_pass.answer: No discrete nodule can be identified and matched on both films, so change in the nodule cannot be judged from these images. The only focal lung abnormality is the hazy right lower zone opacity (F1), present on both films; its size and density cannot be compared because the prior is PA and the current is an underexposed AP, and a new process within it cannot be confirmed or excluded, while the left lung shows no new confluent opacity.

prior_report_discrepancies.prior_report_says: Nodular opacity (no side or zone given).
prior_report_discrepancies.images_show: No discrete, well-defined nodule is seen on the prior or the current film. The prior shows a hazy, ill-defined right lower zone opacity with right hilar and infrahilar prominence (F1, F4). The images cannot establish whether this is the opacity the report means, so it has not been adopted as the nodule. Small nodules cannot be excluded on the underexposed current film.

No definite meniscus or blunted lateral costophrenic angle is seen on either side on the prior or the current film. The right basal contour is high and indistinct medially with an aerated lateral sulcus on both films (F2). Whether this includes subpulmonic fluid remains undetermined on frontal films alone. An effusion has not been adopted as a finding.
